heading: INT. MOON COLONY FUNERAL RECEPTION - EVENING

units.text: INT. MOON COLONY FUNERAL RECEPTION - EVENING
Grey dust drifts past the big round window.
Earth hangs there, small and blue and very far away.
Under the dome, a long table of nutrient cakes nobody is touching.
PIM, a squat round robot the size of a beach ball with two floppy antenna ears, rolls up to the cake table.
Next to him bobs PIP, a thin silver drone with a single blinking eye.
Everyone says they are the same model.
They are not.
Thank you all for coming to say goodbye to Captain Barnaby Tumbleton, who was the best captain of the best crater on the whole moon!
units.name: PIM

units.text: Dust.
Hush.
A distant air pump going whoosh.
Pim, you said "best" twice and he was the only captain.
units.name: PIP

units.text: Then he was twice as best.
units.name: PIM

units.text: The dome lights flicker low.
A tiny sad chime plays from the speakers, and the cake's candle gutters in the thin air.
Pim I miss him.
units.name: PIP

units.text: Me too Pip. (sniff) My antenna ears are leaking.
units.name: PIM

units.text: The airlock hisses.
In rolls AUNT NEBULA, an enormous fluffy purple dust-bunny robot in a black veil, humming slowly.
She stops.
Everything goes still.
Nobody told me I was late. Is there cake left? Is he still dead?
units.name: AUNT NEBULA

units.text: Yes. To both.
units.name: PIM
